text:
It has been a week of milestones in Dallas. Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points, Miro Heiskanen came back from injury and scored the overtime winner in Vegas, and the Stars beat the Golden Knights again Thursday in a shootout. That made four straight wins and a 14-6-2 record good for 30 points.

The results are ahead of the process, though. Dallas gets a modest 52% of the expected goals, our measure of the quality of chances, and in the winning streak only 48%. The goaltending has carried it: the Stars have allowed about 9.6 fewer goals than their chances against suggest. Our numbers say the play has earned about 25 points, so roughly five of the 30 came from saves and good fortune.

Penalties are a quiet problem. Dallas takes 4.18 penalties a game and draws only 3.14, and Thursday the Golden Knights spent most of the second period on the power play. The best regular pair, Thomas Harley and Nils Lundkvist, wins its minutes, and Mikko Rantanen's line with Wyatt Johnston has controlled the chances.

Jason Robertson is the trade-rumor name, with a report saying Pittsburgh came "very close" to a deal. Our playoff odds give Dallas 86%. What we'd watch: whether the chance share catches up to the record before the saves come back to earth.
headline: Dallas is winning more than it's dominating
